title: High-Efficiency Ising Machine with Time-Dimensional Exchange Coupling
authors: Zhengyu Du, Haijie Xu, Kaiming Cai, Zhe Yuan, Yue Zhang
abstract: Conventional probabilistic Ising machines often suffer from inefficient exploration of configuration space, while replica-based quantum Monte Carlo methods reduce sampling bottlenecks at the cost of large hardware overhead. Here we propose a time-dimensional exchange coupling (TEC) that replaces spatial replica coupling with a temporal exchange interaction between successive spin configurations of a single p-bit network. This TEC improves sampling efficiency without duplicating replica hardware. At low temperatures, antiferromagnetic TEC expands sampling range; at high temperatures, ferromagnetic TEC stabilizes the optimal state. For MaxCut problems with up to 2000 vertices, TEC significantly accelerates convergence speed. SPICE simulations confirm hardware feasibility. TEC offers a scalable, hardware-efficient strategy to enhance combinatorial optimization on existing Ising machines.
summary: This work proposes a Time-Dimensional Exchange Coupling (TEC) to enhance the efficiency of solving combinatorial optimization problems like MaxCut on Ising machines. By introducing a temporal interaction between successive spin states, TEC improves sampling exploration at low temperatures and stabilizes solutions at high temperatures. This provides a hardware-efficient alternative to complex replica methods, significantly speeding up convergence.
main_problem: The paper addresses the inefficiency of sampling the configuration space for solving combinatorial optimization problems, such as MaxCut, using probabilistic Ising machines.
main_result: The proposed Time-Dimensional Exchange Coupling (TEC) significantly accelerates convergence speed for MaxCut problems, offering a scalable and hardware-efficient alternative to replica-based quantum Monte Carlo methods.
method: The authors introduce a TEC term into the Ising Hamiltonian, which couples the current spin configuration to the previous one in time, modifying the stochastic dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is based on the Ising model implemented on a p-bit network, simulating the optimization process. The total energy includes both spatial interactions and the novel temporal exchange coupling term, E_total = E_spatial - sum(J_v * sigma_i(t) * sigma_i(t-1)).
key_observables: Convergence speed, solution accuracy (for MaxCut), update velocity, and the shift in optimal TEC coupling strength (J_v) with temperature.
important_parameters: The coupling strength J_v, temperature (T), and the size of the problem (up to 2000 vertices).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the time interval between successive spin configurations is much longer than the spin relaxation time, and the hardware implementation is assumed to be feasible despite minor SPICE simulation inaccuracies.
figures_summary: Figures compare TEC to conventional methods, showing accelerated annealing dynamics for MaxCut; they also illustrate how the optimal TEC coupling strength shifts systematically with temperature.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of existing sampling methods, then introduces the TEC Hamiltonian and dynamics, validates its effect on exploration/stability at different temperatures, and finally benchmarks its performance on large-scale MaxCut problems using both simulation and hardware modeling.
why_interesting: While focused on classical optimization, the dynamics involve time-delayed feedback loops and enhanced sampling mechanisms, which are conceptually related to non-equilibrium dynamics and thermalization processes studied in AMO physics.
